data.title: Install the python package to GAUDI_INSTALL_PYTHONDIR
data.author: jmcarcell
data.body:
BEGINRELEASENOTES
 - Install the k4FWCore python package to `${GAUDI_INSTALL_PYTHONDIR}` instead of the hardcoded `python` directory, so that it ends up in the same directory as the `k4FWCorePluginsConf.py` generated by Gaudi.

ENDRELEASENOTES

The python sources of k4FWCore are installed to a hardcoded `python/k4FWCore`, but the `k4FWCorePluginsConf.py` generated by Gaudi is installed to `${GAUDI_INSTALL_PYTHONDIR}/k4FWCore`. Up to now both were the same directory because Gaudi defaulted `GAUDI_INSTALL_PYTHONDIR` to `python`.

Gaudi v41r0 changes the install layout: plugins (and their `.confdb`/`.components` files) are now installed to `lib/gaudi-plugins` (https://gitlab.cern.ch/gaudi/Gaudi/-/merge_requests/1928), and `GAUDI_INSTALL_PYTHONDIR` defaults to `lib/pythonX.Y/site-packag…

data.title: Fix boolean properties on the k4run command line
data.author: madbaron
data.body:
Boolean properties could not be switched off from the command line:
- when the property is set in the options file, argparse is given type=bool, and bool("False") is True
- when the property is left at its default, its value is propertyNoValue (a string), so the argument is parsed as a string and Gaudi later converts it with bool("False"), which is again True

Parse boolean properties (detected from the value or, if unset, from the default) with a dedicated parser that accepts True/False, true/false and 1/0 and rejects anything else. A bare flag (e.g. "--MetadataSvc.SkipIfSameValue") now means True instead of setting None, which Gaudi converted to False.

Add tests for switching off a property set in the options file, one left at its default, a bare flag and an invalid value.

BEGI…

ENDRELEASENOTES

Nothing changes for existing algorithms, only those using `DataHandles` can pass the `EventContext` now. I left a few tests with the empty `createAndPut()`.

data.title: Simplify the background particle index mapping
data.author: madbaron
data.body:
Follow-up to @davidlange6's review comment in https://github.com/key4hep/k4FWCore/pull/413#discussion_r3933115912. The code it points at predates that PR, so it is split out here against `main`.

`OverlayTiming` built two `std::map`s per background frame to translate background particle indices into output ones. They are redundant: the background particles are cloned in order, so the copy of background particle `i` always lands at `offset + i`.

Dropping them also fixes a guard on the relation wiring: it skipped a relation when the target particle had no relations of its own, rather than when the index pointed outside the background collection. A particle referenced as a daughter whose own parent list is empty, was therefore silently dropped.
